svg.title: LLM inference: shared KV tensor cache
svg.desc:
Reuse exact-prefix attention state; Valkey holds bytes, while GPU memory holds active tensors. The connector uses the runtime import path to copy validated tensors into GPU memory and restore positions and block mappings. The receiving worker uses compatible model weights and runtime layout. Valkey core. Valkey is a backing tier; active attention reads local GPU memory.
Example commands (illustrative, not executed): GET kvt:t42:cfgA:prefixABC:block0 SET kvt:t42:cfgA:prefixABC:block0 <header+K+V-bytes> EX 300 TTL kvt:t42:cfgA:prefixABC:block0
Require exact prefix, compatible model/layout and authorized scope. Valkey stores bytes, not attention compute. Restore to GPU memory; recompute on failure. Transfer can cost more than prefill. Tensor bytes can expose prompt information.
Design assumptions: Conceptual application-managed backing store, not a built-in Valkey feature or a claim of a bundled vLLM connector. Decoder-only causal attention example. K/V blocks are derived from exact tokens plus all preceding context; they are neither model weights nor cached answers nor embedding vectors. Block identity covers tenant/access scope, model weights and adapter revision, exact token prefix including parent context, positions/masks, tokenizer/template effects, and multimodal inputs when present. cfgA and prefixABC are readable stand-ins for validated canonical digests. Tensor compatibility includes per-layer/shard coverage, dtype or quantization, shape, layout, runtime serialization version, and partition mapping. A receiving worker needs compatible weights and a supported import path. Illustrative blocks A/B/C each cover 32 prefix tokens (0-95); block D covers a 32-token suffix (96-127). Each visual K/V pair represents required layer/shard slices, not one model-wide tensor. Use a bounded binary envelope per block/shard containing a validated header plus K and V bytes. Enforce item limits, shape/length checks, integrity and authorization before allocating or restoring. Do not deserialize executable object formats from cache. Complete blocks are published atomically per value. Independent block TTLs can expire: reuse only a complete, validated contiguous prefix; recompute from the first gap. Multi-key atomic publication is not assumed. No per-token remote attention. The runtime retains active state in GPU memory. Benchmark host/device copies, network, validation and restore against avoided prefill; no speedup is promised. Require exact prefix, compatible model/layout and authorized scope. Valkey stores bytes, not attention compute. Restore to GPU memory; recompute on failure. Transfer can cost more than prefill. Tensor bytes can expose prompt information.
